title: Defragmenting Language Models: An Interpretability-based Approach for Vocabulary Expansion
abstract: arXiv:2604.16656v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: All languages are equal; when it comes to tokenization, some are more equal than others. Tokens are the hidden currency that dictates the cost and latency of contemporary LLM access. However, many languages written in non-Latin scripts observe a poor exchange rate: LLMs take several multiples of tokens to encode the same information in many languages as they do for English. We observe that this issue, known as token overfragmentation, persists in modern open-weight LLMs. The standard remedy is vocabulary expansion that adds target language items missing from the model's vocabulary. We focus on two core decisions in the vocabulary expansion process: What items should we add? and How should we initialize their corresponding input and output embeddings? translated_title: 语言模型的碎片整理：一种基于可解释性的词表扩展方法

tldr: 该论文针对LLM在非拉丁文字语言中token过度碎片化的问题，提出了基于可解释性的词表扩展方法，系统研究了“应添加哪些词条”和“如何初始化对应嵌入”这两个核心决策。
en_tdlr: This paper addresses token overfragmentation in LLMs for non-Latin script languages by advancing an interpretability-based vocabulary expansion approach, systematically studying which vocabulary items to add and how to initialize their corresponding embeddings.
